<blocked>The ABI contract requires the driver to call bad(), every time, but bad()'s own implementation is `printLine(helperBad())`, where helperBad() returns the address of its local array `charString` after that array's storage duration has already ended, and the returned dangling pointer is dereferenced by printLine() immediately afterward. That read-through-a-dead-stack-frame is undefined behavior that lives entirely inside the unit's own code (bad() and helperBad()), with no arguments and no driver-visible state to influence it; nothing the driver does before, after, or around the call to bad() can change what happens inside it. Because this UB is intrinsic to a mandatorily-called symbol and outside the driver's control, no driver that satisfies the ABI contract's "call every symbol, every time" requirement can also guarantee output that is identical between -O0 and -O2 builds, which the contract likewise requires.</blocked>
